narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Anatomy Plate"**

One typewriter, drawn as a technical figure on a framed card, is the whole interface. It is a wide typeball electric seen straight from the front: the sheet stays still across the full width of the platen and a small type element travels along it, so a whole line, as many words as fit the width, stays in view at a readable size and on a level baseline. Like a modern typing test, the sheet shows the copy three lines at a time in faint grey: the current line starts at the top, then holds the middle row with the finished line above it and the next line below. The keyboard is drawn at a real machine's scale against the sheet, with each key's letter on its top. The copy is printed faint on the paper, the learner types over it, and the machine answers each key with a stepped mechanical response. Around the figure sit a hairline frame, two bottom captions, a legend under the card, and a quiet bar above it: the brand, two segmented controls for the test length and three icon tools. When the server returns the score, the same card shows the result plate: the machine's figures, a hairline speed chart, a stats row and what to practise next.

The world is monochrome. The bench, card and machine are four-tone grey solids with 0.6px hairline outlines, screws drawn as dots, and ruler ticks cut to the type pitch. Colour exists only as ribbon ink: a black ribbon for correct letters and the red half of a bichrome ribbon for misses, on the paper and, lifted for contrast, on the result plate. The only lit part of the drawing is the strike-point mark. Dark (charcoal bench) and light (paper-white bench) are the same drawing with each tone remapped; the theme follows the system preference and has a toggle.

Density is low and fixed. The card holds a 2.2:1 stage inside whatever height the bar and legend leave, so the machine never scrolls on desktop, and the result plate fills the same stage so nothing jumps when it swaps in. Motion is mechanical, not decorative: the type element jumps one cell with no easing, a strike holds for two frames, and only the return and the line feed glide. The result chart is drawn once like a pen trace.
keyCharacteristics: One anatomy figure, seen from the front, owns the screen; the paper is the test surface: three full lines of copy, faint until typed.
Four-tone monochrome solids, 0.6px hairlines, dots and ticks; no hue outside the ribbon's ink.
One lit part: the strike-point mark.
Courier Prime on the paper, for the machine's figures and for the brand; small system mono for every caption, control and axis.
Square plate, 4px controls with 2px segments, round 17px key discs, flat surfaces.
Stepped motion; reduced motion holds the machine still and draws the chart at once.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Hue appears only as ribbon ink: `ribbon-red` on paper, and `ribbon-red-plate` on the card, where it marks wrong keys and nothing else. The bench, card, machine, controls, captions and every other chart line stay on the grey ramp. The vendored kit's red, green and blue line tones are not part of this world.

rules.name: The One Lit Part Rule
rules.body: The strike-point mark is the only element painted with `lit`. No other solid in the figure is drawn lit, so the eye always finds the print point.

rules.name: The Paired Theme Rule
rules.body: Every colour is declared twice, dark and light, on the same token name; a new tone without a light override is incomplete.

rules.name: The Pitch Cell Rule
rules.body: Every character on paper sits centred in a fixed pitch cell (16.7 units at 28-unit type, 60 columns, wrapped at 56 cells with as many words as fit; the last 4 cells hold extra letters). The scale bar carries one tick per cell. Proportional text never appears on the sheet.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime for paper, the machine's figures and the brand: the sheet, the key labels, the countdown, the result figures, the stat values, the key discs, the typed missed words and "platen", always at 700 off the paper. System mono for everything else: captions, controls, the readout, axis labels, notes. No third family is shown; the sans stack on the page root is a fallback that no visible text uses.

rules.name: The Figures Scale With The Card Rule
rules.body: The countdown and the result figures size in container units of the card (`cqw`), not the window, so they keep their proportion to the drawing.

rules.name: The Drawn Depth Rule
rules.body: Volume belongs to the figure. Interface surfaces stay flat and outlined; the lift stack is reserved for the one transient prompt over the figure.

dos: Do put every reading surface of the test on paper inside the drawing, set in Courier Prime on the pitch grid, with the baseline level; put results on the result plate inside the same card.
Do set the test length as segmented controls and the tools as icon buttons in the bar; show binary tools with `aria-pressed`.
Do declare every new colour as a dark and light pair on the same token name.
Do keep machine motion stepped: one cell per key, two-frame strikes, glides only for the return and the line feed. Result motion is one pen trace and one fade. Nothing moves under reduced motion.
Do keep the plate's captions to the two bottom corners: hint and status readout. No figure numbers or titles.
Do keep chart marks off the wpm gridlines by choosing the error axis top, not by nudging marks.
donts: Don't use hue anywhere but ribbon ink: `ribbon-red` on the sheet, `ribbon-red-plate` for wrong keys on the card. The kit's red, green and blue line tones stay out.
Don't paint a second part of the figure with `lit`; the strike point is the only lit part.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, controls, discs or the tip; depth belongs to the drawing.
Don't set proportional or sans text on the paper, or Courier Prime anywhere but the paper, the machine's figures and the brand; captions, controls and axis labels stay in system mono.
Don't show live wpm or accuracy during the test; the countdown is the only live figure.
Don't use the kit's `muted` grey (#6e6e6e on the card) for text; this build raises captions and legend to `text` for contrast.
